lesson.child_mission: People affect the environment through what they do, such as dropping litter, clearing bush or wasting water. Caring for the environment starts with finding the cause of a problem, seeing its effects on living things and then choosing an action that fits the cause.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Put in order: animals are harmed; litter is dropped; litter washes into the creek. Then name one action that fixes the cause.

FEEDBACK
Litter is dropped, litter washes into the creek, animals are harmed. An action that fits the cause is more bins or a sign at the park entrance.

WATCH FOR
Choosing an action that does not match the cause, such as painting a fence to fix litter, will not solve the problem.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Choose a local environmental problem. Draw a cause and effect chain with at least three links, name two living things affected and propose one safe action with a reason. Use an adult supervised photo or observation as evidence.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
